lesson_lookalike_what: The address you opened imitates a site you trust, with small changes that are easy to miss. Pages like this are built to collect passwords and payments.
lesson_lookalike_habit1: Check the domain, the part right before the first single slash. Small swaps, like rn for m or 0 for o, can hide there.
lesson_lookalike_habit2: If you are not sure, type the address yourself or use your saved bookmark instead of a link.
lesson_lookalike_why: Only paypal.com is PayPal's own address. The others add or swap characters to look similar.
lesson_new_domain_what: This site was registered very recently. Attackers set up new sites for each campaign, so a brand-new address is a reason to slow down.
lesson_new_domain_habit1: Take extra care with a site you have never visited, especially when it asks you to sign in or pay.
lesson_new_domain_habit2: Think about how you got there. If a message or an ad sent you, go to the company's own site instead.
lesson_new_domain_q: A site you have never heard of was registered very recently and asks for your password. What do you do?
lesson_new_domain_a: Leave, and go to the company's known address myself
lesson_new_domain_w1: Sign in, then check whether the page looks right
lesson_new_domain_w2: Enter a made-up password to test it
lesson_new_domain_why: A new site can look perfect. Reaching the company through an address you already trust is safer than judging the page.
lesson_reported_what: This site has been reported by security researchers as phishing or malware. Reports like this come from people who have examined the site.
lesson_reported_habit1: Treat a warning about a reported site as reliable, even when the page looks professional.
lesson_reported_habit2: Do not sign in, download, or call numbers shown on it. Tell your security team if a message sent you there.
lesson_reported_q: The page looks polished, but researchers have reported it. What should you do?
lesson_reported_w1: Trust the design, since it looks real
lesson_reported_w2: Continue, but use a different password
lesson_reported_why: How a page looks proves nothing. Reported sites are often copies of real ones.
lesson_download_what: This file type can run code on your computer, and it comes from a site we flagged. Opening it could give someone else control of your device.
lesson_download_habit1: Only keep files you asked for, from a source you trust.
lesson_download_habit2: Take most care with programs, scripts and archives, even when the name says invoice or document.
lesson_download_q: You did not ask for this file, and it came from a flagged site. What do you do?
lesson_download_w1: Keep it and scan it later
lesson_download_w2: Open it once to see what it is
lesson_download_why: Some files run the moment you open them. Decide before you keep it, not after.
lesson_consent_what: Imagine an app you have not verified asking for permission to read your mail. If you agree, it can read your messages without asking for your password again.
lesson_consent_habit1: Before you allow an app, check who made it and whether you expected the request.
lesson_consent_habit2: Be careful with permissions to read mail or files, and with publishers you do not know. If unsure, ask your IT team.
lesson_consent_q: An unverified app asks to read your mail. What do you do?
lesson_consent_a: Decline and ask my IT team
lesson_consent_w1: Allow it, I can remove it later
lesson_consent_w2: Allow it if the app name sounds familiar
lesson_consent_why: Access you grant stays active until someone removes it, and a familiar name is easy to copy.
lesson_aipaste_what: Imagine pasting an API key into an AI tool. Text you paste can be stored by the tool and seen by other people.
lesson_aipaste_habit1: Keep keys, passwords and customer data out of AI tools. Swap them for placeholders first.
lesson_aipaste_habit2: If a secret was pasted, treat it as exposed: replace it and tell your security team.
lesson_aipaste_q: You want help debugging code that contains an API key. What do you do?
lesson_aipaste_a: Replace the key with a placeholder, then paste
lesson_aipaste_w1: Paste it as it is, the tool is private
lesson_aipaste_w2: Paste it and delete the chat afterwards
lesson_aipaste_why: Deleting a chat does not always remove what was shared. Leave secrets out from the start.
lesson_done_body: That is the whole lesson. Next time, take a moment before you sign in or download.
